title: She wasn’t dying…
paragraphs:
She wasn’t dying…
but it felt like something inside her was.

And instead of distracting herself—
she asked God why.
That alone will confront most of us.
Because when the pressure rises, we don’t seek God first… we seek relief.

Rebekah felt a war in her own body.
Not external. Not visible. Internal. Violent. Confusing.
Genesis 25:22 says the children struggled together within her, and she cried out, “If all is well, why is this happening to me?”
That question?
That’s not rebellion.
That’s honesty.
But here’s the tension nobody talks about…

She didn’t run to people first.
She didn’t numb the discomfort.
She went to inquire of the Lord.
And that’s where most of us quietly fail.

We carry spiritual tension…
but we treat it like emotional inconvenience.

We feel conviction…
but we rename it stress.

We sense God stirring something deeper…
but we silence it with noise, distractions, or delayed obedience.
Let me ask you something—be honest:

When something inside you feels off…
do you actually bring it to God?
Or do you wait until it breaks you?

Some of us are not confused.
We are just avoiding the voice of God.
Read that again.

Rebekah didn’t understand what she was carrying…
but she understood where to go.
And God answered her.

Not with comfort first—
but with truth.
He told her, “Two nations are in your womb…” (Genesis 25:23)

In other words:
“What you feel isn’t random. It’s spiritual.”
AHA REVELATION:

Not every internal struggle is a sign something is wrong.
Sometimes it’s a sign something significant is happening.
But here’s the mirror most people won’t face—
SPIRITUAL MIRROR STATEMENT:

If you never seek God about what’s happening inside you,
you will mislabel spiritual battles as personal problems.
And you will fight the wrong war.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.

Some people pray only when things fall apart.
Others go to God—but only after they’ve already decided what they want Him to say.
That’s not surrender.
That’s negotiation.

And God is not a consultant you hire to confirm your feelings.
He is Lord.
Here’s the truth that cuts:
You can be close to God’s promise… and still handle your struggle in your own strength.
Rebekah could have done that.
But she didn’t.
She sought the Lord.
Now don’t miss this—because this is where grace breaks in.

Rebekah’s life wasn’t perfect after this.
Later, she would manipulate outcomes, rush God’s promise, and create tension in her own family.
And that sounds a lot like us.

We seek God in one moment…
and struggle to trust Him in the next.
This is why the story doesn’t end with Rebekah.
It points forward.
To Jesus.

Because the deeper issue isn’t just confusion.
It’s sin.

It’s the quiet pride that says, “I’ll figure it out.”
It’s the hidden resistance that delays obedience.
It’s the subtle belief that we can manage life without fully surrendering.
Scripture says in Proverbs 3:5–6, “Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding…”
But we lean anyway.
And that’s why we need a Savior.

Jesus didn’t just come to give answers.
He came to rescue us from the very nature that keeps running from God.

On the cross, He carried not just our sins—
but our confusion, our self-reliance, our silent rebellion.

And through His resurrection, He made a way for us not just to survive struggle—
but to be transformed in it.
Grace doesn’t just comfort you.
It confronts you… then restores you.
Conviction line:

Some of us want God to explain our struggle…
but we don’t want Him to expose our surrender.
That’s where repentance begins.
Not just saying sorry.
But turning.
Returning.
Releasing control.
You are not called to figure everything out.
You are called to seek Him first.
Identity shift:

You are not a person ruled by confusion.
You are a child invited into divine clarity.

You are not abandoned in your struggle.
You are being drawn into deeper dependence.
So here’s the invitation—

What is happening inside you right now…
that you haven’t brought to God yet?

The tension.
The questions.
The quiet unrest.
Bring it.
Not later.
Now.
Not as information… but as formation.
Because surface faith will not sustain you in deep struggle.
If this pierced you, don’t ignore it.
And stay close.
Follow if you’re ready to grow.
Because the next message might be the one that answers the question you haven’t said out loud yet.
